model_rendering.renderer: Three.js models in a shared MapLibre geographic WebGL layer; eye-level inspection uses the same map camera. Source plans use the inline SVG canvas.
model_rendering.selection: Source feature IDs retained. Model camera focus is a display operation. Source image/tracing remains independently available.

dimensions.abu-saraj-iv17: Plan 5 scale, 3 m / 178 sampled pixels. Uniform height 1.55 m within reported 1.4–1.7 m. Roof cap, rock thickness, masonry height and scan sampling illustrative.
dimensions.hyrcania-waterworks: Northern pool floor at -5 m, southern member at -2.6 m; approximate published northern sides. Rock separation 5.1 m within reported 4.8–5.4 m. Southern footprint, bridge, summit and other cistern dimensions illustrative.
dimensions.gerizim-precinct: Reported 212 × 136 m enclosure, 40 × 40 m mansion, 20 × 14 m building IV, 25 × 24 m citadel. East stair uses maximum 23 m width, 34 m run, 15.5 m rise and approximately 57 steps. Western landing distinct from southern seven-step and E1 flights. Other heights, divisions, cistern and platform relief illustrative.
dimensions.jericho-early: Approximate 18 × 13 m pool envelopes; 2.5 m depth, columns and platform illustrative.
dimensions.jericho-late: Approximate 32 × 18 m joined envelope; 2.5 m depth, columns and platform illustrative.
dimensions.relative_models: Doq, Qumran, Siloam and Area AC are normalized relative frames. Heights/depths and channel cross-sections illustrative; selection envelopes are not measured footprints.

model_rendering.orientation: Source frame relationships retained or simplified as documented; no geographic registration or additional compass bearing inferred.
model_rendering.interpretation: Display geometry and materials are illustrative; consult each feature evidence record and model assumptions.

landscape.method: Modern elevation sampled around existing site anchors, with a feathered display bench and source-qualified architectural volumes. Terrain is contextual; footprint placement and compass bearing are illustrative. IV/17 uses an illustrative setting without coordinates.

surface_art.method: Original deterministic 512-pixel colour and relief/roughness tiles, projected in world metres. Separate masonry, limestone, stratified bedrock, soil and plaster treatments. Physical chipped stone courses, coping, open channel troughs, grounded rubble and sparse vegetation; no publication or photograph pixels are used as texture maps. Dominant-axis projection uses one texture sample per map and avoids blending away sharp material detail.

profiles.Qumran: Warm fractured limestone and dusty ground; connected rock beds and a shaded angular recess replace floating rounded rocks.
profiles.Doq: Ochre limestone and rough desert masonry around the plan-derived cistern/channel relations.
profiles.Hyrcania: Cream limestone and muted plaster distinguish the paired basins.
profiles.Jericho: Warm stone, reddish soil and pale worn plaster; source states remain separate.
profiles.Gerizim: Cooler ashlar palette and sparse sage vegetation around the precinct/stair relationships.
profiles.Siloam: Grey-gold limestone and muted plaster around the small receiving-basin tracing.

inspected_material_references.scope: Visible fractured stone, granular soil and outlet recess; illustrative material and opening-form comparison only, without camera registration or inferred hidden architecture.
Limestone grain and surface wear only. Photograph is the larger southern stepped pool; its steps, walls and dimensions are not transferred to the small receiving-basin model.
Escarpment colour and exposed relief character; regional visual context, not a measured local cliff model.

surface_art.evidence_limit: Palette, chipping, individual stone joints, cliff bedding, plaster wear, rubble, vegetation, light and sky are illustrative surface art. These additions supply no new archaeological observations, dimensions, phase assignments or identification evidence.
surface_art.rendering: Directional sun, hemisphere fill, ACES tone mapping, static shadow map, eye-level sky; 2048-pixel desktop / 1024-pixel phone shadow atlas. Repeated masonry and scree use GPU instancing. Thin soil floors receive shadows without casting self-shadow artifacts. Regional source layers pause at eye level and regain their individual visibility on exit; the site and sky continue rendering in the same geographic canvas.
surface_art.camera: Initial eye-level positions frame a source feature such as the eastern stair, pool rim or channel. These are display viewpoints, not surveyed camera positions or walking routes. Eye-level look can pass above the horizon to inspect cliff faces and tall structures; exiting restores the normal geographic camera limits.
surface_art.covered_passages: The normalized Reeder–Jol scene uses angular rock-cut display sections in place of smooth tubes. Their rectangular roof section is illustrative. A copper-coloured lining retains the proposed-course distinction in the source.

unified_map.walking: Eye-level free inspection camera, 1.7 m above modeled ground; ground follows the display surface. Wall collisions, a surveyed navigation mesh and a verified ancient walking route are not supplied.
unified_map.photos: Original licensed source JPEGs are archived with provenance at research/assets/plans/atlas-ground-photographs; matching atlas mirror and public copies retain identical bytes, authors and license links.

unified_map.access: No fresh private Google Drive file retrieval or live YouTube playback verification is claimed. Inline Drive preview uses the viewer account permissions; provider domains are saved in the environment draft.
unified_map.validation: Production GitHub Pages build served locally to Chromium with software WebGL. Desktop and phone checks cover all mapped sites, rendered source geometry, one persistent geographic canvas, inline plan/photo/Drive/video references, eye-level movement, looking above the horizon and return to map. Switching sites with references open preserves the explicit selection and closes the panel. IV/17 checks cover the original figure, visible feature list, pillar evidence and citations, inline Hebrew/English passage, close/reopen and legacy source/model/walk aliases without an invented map pin. External services were deliberately blocked in these tests; live provider coverage, private Drive access, hardware frame rates and GitHub Pages deployment are not established. Public-site and Pages API requests returned proxy 403 Forbidden; no tool to control the user’s Mac Chrome was available. Simplified-header browser checks confirm Evidence/Map/Scroll links fit desktop and phone, the source catalogue and comparison retain entry context, historical maps open through Options and the More menu is absent. Walking-control checks now click the figure with the IV/17 plan open, verify its unplaced-site explanation and test a shorter phone viewport. Supported-site regression enters eye level while Sources is open, confirming that the panel cannot block walking.

reference_panel.content: The original source figure or project tracing, numbered feature list, feature description, interpretation limits, citations and expandable Hebrew/English entry text are native atlas panel content. The former standalone explorer and its duplicated view switch/mobile drawer are removed.
reference_panel.interaction: Plan selection, feature focus, zoom and reading preserve the geographic map canvas. The panel has Plan, Photos and Sources; site videos share Photos. Historical maps open through map Options. Map menus stay accessible above the panel; selecting a different site closes it. Automatic nearby-site selection applies to direct map gestures only, so camera restoration and panel padding cannot undo an explicit site choice.
reference_panel.iv17: The Sion 2002 Plan 5 figure (p. 63), openings, pillar and related entry 25 text are accessible inside the atlas. Legacy source/model/walk URLs open the plan because this candidate has no established geographic location. No invented map position or map-based walking route is assigned.
reference_panel.provenance: Reuses the existing plan, feature and text records, including attribution, original caption/scale/north arrow, source limits and the indexed Copper Scroll Drive reference. This interface integration supplies no new archaeological observations.

unified_map.navigation: The shared header has Evidence, Map and Scroll. The More menu and duplicate section links are removed. Sources and research comparisons stay within Evidence. The site panel has Plan, Photos and Sources; videos share Photos, while historical maps open from map Options. Legacy research bookmarks remain valid.
unified_map.walking_control: A filled yellow figure labeled Walk remains visible and clickable alongside a desktop reference panel and above the phone sheet. Clicking it at an unplaced candidate explains the missing map location; no location or walking coverage is invented. Supported site models enter eye level directly with reference material open.
unified_map.publication: Root _config.yml explicitly includes atlas-site and excludes atlas/, research/ and images/. Jekyll 3.10 EntryFilter treats literal paths as prefixes and applies include before exclude: the previous exclude: atlas setting also excluded atlas-site, omitting the scripts and styles referenced by the homepage. The revised payload checker reproduces that rejection with the old config and stages the surviving static files with the corrected config. Chromium loads the staged bare /CopperScroll/ homepage and site deep links on desktop and phone without missing local assets. Archives remain in GitHub; the filtered payload is about 72 MiB. Hosted deployment remains unverified because requests to the public site return proxy 403 Forbidden.
